key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 tunes the electronic structure and photovoltaic performance dramatically, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the best solar absorber and Ca3PF3 the weakest.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a composition-driven design route for perovskite solar materials, enabling targeted bandgap and efficiency optimization through halide engineering.
method: First-principles investigation of structural, electronic, and optical properties
Band structure analysis to determine direct bandgaps
SLME-based screening to estimate photovoltaic suitability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps of 2.0eV to 3.788eV and SLME results up to 29.6% for Ca3PI3 versus 0.6% for Ca3PF3.
watch_item: These are computational screening results, so experimental synthesis stability, defects, and device-level losses still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
